can_do: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) of main lexical verbs with auxiliary 'do'.
examples: Do you remember Julie? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)
Did you buy a new mobile phone? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)
[talking about a computer] I’m not using it any more. (A2 Turkish)
…the fridge isn't working. (Romanian, ===NONE===, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2009)
… he's going to work at 5.00 am, so he's not eating anything ... (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Polish; Pass)

can_do: Can use the past simple passive affirmative after a singular subject.
examples: It was built in 1880. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Chinese; Pass)
On Saturday morning I was invited to a sports competition. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Tamil; Pass)

can_do: Can use the past simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects both singular and plural.
examples: It was written in a strange language that I tried to translate. (B1 Spanish - Latin American)
Next day, I heard that my neighbour's car was stolen. (B1 Polish)
They filmed the flowers and trees, and some pupils were interviewed about their work in the garden, too. (B1 German)

can_do: Can use the affirmative form with 'like'.
examples: I'd like to invite you to dinner. (Farsi, A1 BREAKTHROUGH, Pass, 2008)
I would like to eat some Spanish food. (Italian, A1 BREAKTHROUGH, Pass, 2006)
